records.section_heading: Bacterial community dynamics are linked to patterns of coral heat tolerance
records.question: Does exposure to thermal bleaching conditions change the microbiome of heat-sensitive corals but not heat-tolerant corals?
records.ground_truth_answer: Yes. Exposing these corals to thermal bleaching conditions changes the microbiome for heat-sensitive corals, but not for heat-tolerant corals growing in habitats with natural high heat extremes.
ground_truth_chunks: Exposing these corals to thermal bleaching conditions changes the microbiome for heat-sensitive corals, but not for heat-tolerant corals growing in habitats with natural high heat extremes.
Subsequent exposure of these corals to thermal bleaching conditions changes the microbial community of heat-sensitive corals coming from a more stable, cooler environment.

records.question: After 17 months of reciprocal transplantation, were the microbiomes of non-native corals transplanted into each pool distinguishable from the microbiomes of the native corals in the same pool?
records.ground_truth_answer: No — 17 months after transplantation, the microbiomes of non-native corals transplanted into each pool could not be distinguished from the microbiomes of the native corals in the same pool (ANOSIM, HV pool R = 0.013, MV pool R = 0.005, both P > 0.05).
ground_truth_chunks: Reciprocal transplantation of coral colonies between the two thermally distinct environments strikingly demonstrated that coral microbial communities fully adjusted to the new environmental conditions: 17 months after transplantation, the microbiomes of non-native corals transplanted into each pool could not be distinguished from the microbiomes of the native corals in the same pool (Fig. 1c, ANOSIM, HV pool  $R\!=\!0.013$ , MV pool  $R\!=\!0.005$ , both  $P\!>\!0.05$ ).

At the same time, cross-transplanted fragments were significantly different from their back-transplanted (genet) counterparts (Fig. 1c, ANOSIM, HV pool  $R\!=\!0.149$ ,  $P\!<\!0.005$ , MV pool  $R\!=\!0.184$ ,  $P\!<\!0.001$ ).

records.question: How many functional traits and proteins distinguished the microbial communities between the HV and MV coral pools?

Functional profiles of microbial communities were distinct between HV and MV corals (Table 1).

records.question: After 17 months of reciprocal transplantation between the HV and MV pools, did microbiomes of non-native Acropora hyacinthus corals adjust to the new environmental conditions and become similar to native corals in the same pool?
records.ground_truth_answer: Yes. After 17 months of transplantation, microbiomes of non-native corals adjusted to the new environmental conditions and were not significantly different from native corals in the same pool.
ground_truth_chunks: Native coral colonies in the two pools had different microbial communities. Moreover, after 17 months of transplantation, microbiomes of non-native corals transplanted into each pool adjusted to the new environmental conditions and were not significantly different from native corals in the same pool.

Nevertheless, while we did not transfer microbiomes between HV and MV corals, the long-term transplantation effectively resulted in HV corals harbouring an MV microbiome and MV corals harbouring an HV microbiome associated with higher and lower susceptibility to coral bleaching, respectively.
